gpt.text:
Run the three “Next Commands” in order; they’re set up to (1) explore module-level candidates and pick the best, (2) explore system-level candidates, and (3) generate a targeted “next fix” report based on the latest runs.

## 1) Module autopilot (AUB) — run + select best
```bash
python3 experiment_system/tools/aub_autopilot.py \
  --registry experiment_system/config/module_registry.yaml \
  --run --select-best
```
What this should do:
- Execute the AUB experiment sweep defined by `module_registry.yaml`
- Compare candidates against the current champion (`baseline/champion_v5_latest.json`)
- If any candidate **passes**, it should promote/select it as best (depending on how your tool implements “select-best”)

What to verify after it finishes:
- A report/artifact indicating which candidate (if any) was selected
- Whether a new “champion” file was written/updated, or if it only records selection in a run directory

## 2) System autopilot — system candidate sweep
```bash
python3 experiment_system/tools/system_autopilot.py \
  --spec experiment_system/config/system_candidates.yaml \
  --run
```
What this should do:
- Run end-to-end system candidate configurations from `system_candidates.yaml`
- Produce comparable metrics to the “tuning_mean/min” and “lockbox_mean/min” you listed

What to verify:
- Any candidate marked PASS / FAIL / INCONCLUSIVE
- Whether any candidate improves lockbox (usually the harder-to-game metric) without regressing tuning beyond your thresholds

## 3) Generate next fix recommendations
```bash
python3 experiment_system/tools/aub_next_fix.py \
  --registry experiment_system/config/module_registry.yaml \
  --output baseline/reports/next_fix.md
```
What this should do:
- Look at the most recent AUB outcomes
- Emit a concrete “what to try next” plan into `baseline/reports/next_fix.md` (e.g., which modules are bottlenecking, what variants to add, etc.)

## If something goes wrong (quick triage)
- If you see no PASS candidates: check whether the tool is generating INCONCLUSIVE due to insufficient samples, timeouts, or statistical thresholds.
- If “select-best” doesn’t update the champion automatically: search run outputs for a “best candidate” path/id and manually promote via your project’s champion-update mechanism (if one exists).
- If lockbox improves but tuning regresses: confirm your selection logic prioritizes lockbox (or whichever metric is meant to be primary).

If you paste the stdout summaries (or the produced report paths), I can help interpret which candidate (if any) should be promoted and what the next fix is likely to recommend.
